topics.label: Course Introduction and Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and outlines how familiar immune components will be examined in mechanistic detail.

topics.label: Principles of Pathogen and Damage Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the essential properties of pathogen-associated and damage-associated molecular patterns and explain the germline encoding and cellular localization of pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Signaling Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the major families of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling pathways, and the assembly of the inflammasome to activate inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Sentinel Cell Activation and Leukocyte Recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated sentinel cells induce vascular endothelial adhesion molecules to coordinate the rolling, extravasation, and chemokine-directed migration of leukocytes to the site of infection.

topics.label: Lymphatic Drainage and Antigen Transport
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tissue fluid drainage through the lymphatic system enables dendritic cells to carry antigens to lymph nodes for the activation of adaptive immunity.

topics.label: Systemic Hyperinflammation and Septic Shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the life-threatening consequences of uncontrolled cytokine release causing widespread vasodilation and septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the passive and active mechanisms that resolve acute inflammation, the process of tissue repair, and the development of chronic inflammation and protective granulomas.
